what_its_for: Cladribine is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including relapsing-remitting MS and active secondary progressive MS, in adults who have not responded well to or cannot tolerate other MS medicines. It works by reducing the number of certain immune cells (lymphocytes) that attack the nervous system. An injectable form (Leustatin) is also used to treat a type of blood cancer called hairy cell leukemia.
how_to_take: Cladribine tablets (Mavenclad) are taken by mouth. Swallow the tablet whole with water — do not chew, crush, or split it. Take it at the same time each day during your treatment week. You can take it with or without food. If you are taking more than one tablet on a given day, you may take them together or separately, but at least 3 hours apart. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after handling the tablet. Do not share your tablets with anyone else.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight. The total treatment is spread over 2 years. In Year 1 and Year 2, you take a short course of tablets during 2 separate weeks (called treatment weeks), usually about 4 weeks apart. After completing both years, no further cladribine is needed for at least the next 2 years. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing schedule exactly — do not change the dose or schedule on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose on a given day, take it on the following day and then continue your schedule as planned — this may extend your treatment week by one day. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, contact your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store cladribine tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original package to protect them from moisture. Keep all medicines out of the reach and sight of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any leftover tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live or live-attenuated vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) during treatment and for at least 4 to 6 weeks after your last dose in each treatment year — ask your doctor when it is safe. Avoid close contact with people who have active infections, especially chickenpox or shingles. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose in each treatment year, as cladribine can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 1 week after the last dose of each treatment week. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have any vision changes.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, painful urination, or sores that do not heal; unusual bruising or bleeding; extreme tiredness or weakness; swollen lymph nodes; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain; skin rash or blisters; mouth sores; shortness of breath; or any signs of a new or worsening neurological problem. Also call your doctor before any vaccinations, surgeries, or dental procedures while on this medicine.
when_it_works: Cladribine does not work overnight. Most patients begin to notice fewer MS relapses within the first few months of treatment. The full benefit of reducing relapses and slowing disability is usually seen over the course of 1 to 2 years of treatment. Keep all follow-up appointments and lab tests your doctor schedules, as blood tests are needed regularly to monitor your immune cell counts and overall health.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use cladribine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Women of childbearing age and male partners of women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose of each treatment year. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or the medicine may not be suitable for you. Children and teenagers: Cladribine tablets are not approved for use in people under 18 years of age. Older adults: Use with caution in older patients; your doctor will assess whether this medicine is appropriate for you. HIV or immune system problems: This medicine is not recommended if you have HIV infection or any condition that severely weakens your immune system.
